audited_claim: For every finite simple cyclic graph F, (C4,F) has both properties in Erdős problem #596 if and only if girth(F) >= 5.
assumptions: F is finite and contains at least one cycle.
The ambient set theory is ZFC, as in the cited arbitrary-cardinal graph result.

nesetril_rodl_input.finding: Reiher-Rödl Theorem 2.1 states the required edge-Ramsey result for every graph F of girth >4 and every integer r>=2, with a host H of girth >4. The r=1 case is immediate with H=F.

erdos_hajnal_decomposition.finding: Erdős-Hajnal Theorem 10 applies to graphs of arbitrary cardinality and gives a type-omega edge-decomposition into acyclic spanning subgraphs. Their word 'tree' means an acyclic graph, i.e. a modern forest; it is not merely a countable overlapping cover.

triangle_obstruction.finding: Triangles in a C4-free graph are pairwise edge-disjoint. Well-ordering the edges gives a conflict-free global two-coloring in which each triangle has one red and two blue edges.

cyclic_trichotomy.finding: The disjoint cases girth 3, girth 4, and girth at least 5 exhaust every finite cyclic simple graph.

counterexample_search.scope: Elementary triangle and trichotomy branches only; external structural theorems are source-audited rather than computationally tested.

required_report_corrections: Describe Erdős-Hajnal as an omega edge-decomposition into forests, not an overlapping cover by connected trees.
Cite Reiher-Rödl Theorem 2.1 exactly and handle r=1 separately.
Make the global triangle coloring explicit using a well-order.
State the cyclic split as the mutually exclusive girth 3 / girth 4 / girth >=5 trichotomy.
